Yes—the quantity closest to our current goal is the curvature after removing the two zeros we are tracking. If \(A=G_N/[(z-z_1)(z-z_2)]\), then at a double zero the desired sign is
\[
-K=\frac{(A')^2-AA''}{A^2}>0.
\]
That makes the deflated expression \((A')^2-AA''\) a more relevant candidate for grouping. I’ll work out its connection to the Fourier terms and distinguish a useful local bound from a restatement of the unknown sign.

The calculation gives a concrete Fourier target: at an exact double, the sign depends on \(2(G_N''')^2-3G_N''G_N''''\). Pairing its frequency terms produces a positive constant part and an oscillatory remainder. A simple positive-weight Jacobi example makes the total negative at a double, so a useful proof will need additional information about the actual theta source’s phases.

Yes. **The quantity most directly suited to this idea is the logarithmic curvature after removing the two zeros we are tracking.**

Write
\[
G_N(z)=(z-z_1)(z-z_2)A_N(z).
\]
Then consider
\[
\mathcal C_N(z)
=-\left(\frac{A_N'}{A_N}\right)'
=\frac{(A_N')^2-A_NA_N''}{A_N^2}.
\]
For a real pair, \(-K_N\) is the average of \(\mathcal C_N\) along the segment joining the zeros. At a double zero \(c\), it is simply \(\mathcal C_N(c)\). Thus a positive lower bound measures the favorable exterior interaction we want.

There is a concrete Fourier expression to investigate. At an exact double, Taylor expansion gives
\[
-K_N(c)=
\frac{\mathcal P_N(c)}{18G_N''(c)^2},
\qquad
\mathcal P_N=2(G_N''')^2-3G_N''G_N''''.
\]
Substituting your spectral sum yields
\[
\mathcal P_N(z)=\frac12\sum_{j,k}
\omega_j\omega_k x_j^2x_k^2
\bigl(3x_j^2-4x_jx_k+3x_k^2\bigr)
e^{iz(x_j+x_k)}.
\]

This gives a natural organization: **group by the frequency sums \(x_j+x_k\), then pair opposite sums.** All the spectral coefficients are nonnegative because
\[
3x_j^2-4x_jx_k+3x_k^2
=x_j^2+x_k^2+2(x_j-x_k)^2.
\]
Opposite nodes contribute a positive constant; the remaining groups are cosine terms whose correlations still matter. This belongs to the established Fourier–Laguerre framework. [Csordas](https://arxiv.org/html/1309.0055v2)

The missing ingredient is substantial: positive coefficients alone do not make the oscillatory sum positive. I checked an explicit positive-weight Jacobi example where this numerator is negative at a double. A successful grouping therefore needs additional information about the actual source’s frequencies and phases.

So your corrected suggestion gives us a precise research target: **group the Fourier terms of the normalized deflated curvature and control the complete signed remainder.** The same numerator also has a direct complete-source integral formula, so we need not restrict the idea to finite \(N\).
